c11_acc_cbse_03_005: Expenses and assets both take debits, but expenses shrink capital while assets are resources owned. Prepaid rent is an asset until the benefit is used up.
c12_acc_cbse_03_006: Mid-year, final profit isn't known — debit P&L Suspense for the deceased partner's estimated share, and close it to P&L Appropriation at year-end.
c11_acc_cbse_03_006: The bank is a separate legal entity, so Bank is a Personal account, not Real. Drawings is Personal too — it's the owner's own account, not an expense.
c12_acc_cbse_03_007: Only the policy's surrender value sat in the books — the excess claim over it is a profit shared by all partners in their ratio, including the deceased's share.
c11_acc_cbse_03_007: In the manual journal, the credit account goes on the next line, indented with 'To'. Software displays compress it — exam format doesn't.
c12_acc_cbse_03_008: Use capital balances after all retirement adjustments — goodwill, revaluation, reserves — and subtract the retiring partner's paid-off capital before finding the new capitals.
c11_acc_cbse_03_008: In a compound entry, total debits must equal total credits — not each pair. Check the sums, not pairwise matches.
c12_acc_cbse_03_009: JLP proceeds aren't automatically all the deceased's — the split depends on how the policy was kept: at surrender value, sum assured, or unrecorded.
c11_acc_cbse_03_009: The ledger isn't a copy of the journal — it accumulates. Five sales to Mohan become five debits in one account with a running balance.
c12_acc_cbse_03_010: Goodwill on retirement adjusts in the gaining ratio (new share − old share), not the new ratio. Work out each continuing partner's gain first.
c11_acc_cbse_03_010: In the Particulars column, name the other account in the transaction — the ledger already knows its own title. Write the source or destination, not itself.
c12_acc_cbse_04_001: A partner joining, retiring or dying reconstitutes the firm — it doesn't dissolve the business. Revaluation Account, not Realisation, is what you prepare.
c11_acc_cbse_03_011: Balance c/d always goes on the shorter side — for liabilities and capital that's the debit side. Check which side is smaller before placing it.
c12_acc_cbse_04_002: A written deed isn't required — a partnership can arise orally or by conduct (Section 5), becoming a partnership at will. Check conduct, not just paperwork.
c11_acc_cbse_04_001: The cash book needs a narration and the L.F. holds the ledger page, not its own. And it records cash only — a credit sale never enters it.
c12_acc_cbse_04_003: Realisation Account never handles partners' capital directly — it tracks asset sales and liability payments. Settlement goes through Capital and Bank accounts.
c11_acc_cbse_04_002: Discount columns are nominal — total them and post to the ledger; there's no balance c/d. Only real and personal accounts carry balances down.
c12_acc_cbse_04_004: Who pays isn't who bears — the agreement decides who bears the expense; the payer only decides what gets credited (Bank or the partner's Capital).
c11_acc_cbse_04_003: The reimbursement restores the float — record it in the main cash book (debit Petty Cash, credit Bank), not again on the petty book's receipts side.
c12_acc_cbse_04_005: At dissolution the books are closing — don't first bring unrecorded items into the ledger. Realisation captures the gain or loss directly.
c11_acc_cbse_04_004: Purchases Book takes credit purchases of goods for resale only — cash purchases go to Cash Book, asset purchases to Journal Proper. Check both qualifiers.
c12_acc_cbse_04_006: A partner's loan is a liability, not part of capital — settle it before capital, and its interest is a charge, not an appropriation.
c11_acc_cbse_04_005: On purchase return, debit the Supplier (liability shrinks) and credit Purchases Return. Think from your firm's books, not the supplier's.
c12_acc_cbse_04_007: Partner's loan ranks above partner's capital under Section 48 — pay the creditor hat before the owner hat, even though it's the same person.
c11_acc_cbse_04_006: Journal Proper isn't just for rare entries — opening, closing and transfer entries go there every year, plus any credit purchase that isn't goods for resale.
c12_acc_cbse_04_008: In CBSE/NCERT an insolvent partner's deficiency is borne in the profit-sharing ratio, not the capital ratio — that's the English Garner v Murray rule.
c11_acc_cbse_04_007: Purchases, Sales and Returns books hold nominal items — total and transfer them to Trading/P&L. They aren't balanced with Balance c/d like the Cash Book.
c12_acc_cbse_04_009: Realisation Account takes assets and liabilities at book value — the gap between book and realised value is the profit or loss on realisation.
